request: how does a bill become law in the United States?

composition.story: A bill travels from initial proposal through committee review, floor debate, and presidential signature to become law.

aha.observation: Only after presidential approval or a successful veto override does the bill finally become official law.

states.label: Introduction
states.why: Bills start their journey in the hopper of either chamber.

states.label: Committee
states.sentence: Committees review and amend the bill.
states.why: Experts examine details and hold hearings.

states.label: Floor Debate
states.sentence: The chamber debates and votes on passage.
states.why: Amendments are added and final chamber approval is tested.

states.label: Second Chamber
states.sentence: The bill passes through the second chamber.
states.why: Both House and Senate must pass identical text.

states.label: Conference
states.why: Resolves discrepancies between House and Senate versions.

states.label: Presidential Action
states.sentence: The President signs the bill into law.
states.why: Final executive check completes the legislative enactment.
